readmeExcerpt:
eve

[eve](https://eve.dev/) is a filesystem-first framework for durable AI agents. Core agent capabilities live in conventional locations, so projects are easier to inspect, extend, and operate. ## The filesystem is the authoring interface A typical eve agent has this structure: ```text my-agent/ └── agent/ ├── agent.ts # Optional: model and runtime config ├── instructions.md # Required: the always-on system prompt ├── tools/ # Optional: typed functions the model can call │ └── get_weather.ts ├── skills/ # Optional: procedures loaded on demand │ └── plan_a_trip.md ├── channels/ # Optional: message channels (HTTP, Slack, Discord) │ └── slack.ts └── schedules/ # Optional: recurring cron jobs └── weekly_recap.ts ``` Read the [documentation](https://eve.dev/docs) for the full project layout and guides. ## Quick start ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent ``` This creates a new `my-agent` directory, installs its dependencies, initializes Git, and starts the interactive terminal UI. The generated agent uses `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` with high reasoning. To start with another AI Gateway model, pass its model ID: ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra ``` Passing `--model` without `--reasoning` uses the provider's default reasoning. Pass `--reasoning` to set it explicitly. To add eve to an existing project, pass a path: ```bash cd myapp npx eve@latest init . ``` > [!NOTE] > The `eve` package includes its full documentation, so coding agents can read it locally from > `node_modules/eve/docs`. ### A minimal example The generated project includes an `agent` directory. Replace `agent/instructions.md` with: ```md You are a concise weather demo assistant. Tell users that the weather data is mocked. ``` Add a mock weather tool at `agent/tools/get_weather.ts`: ```ts import { defineTool } from "eve/tools"; import { z } from "zod"; export default defineTool({ description: "Return mock weather data for a city.", inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string().min(1) }), async execute({ city }) { return { city, condition: "Sunny", temperatureF: 72 }; }, }); ``` Choose the model in `agent/agent.ts`: ```ts import { defineAgent } from "eve"; export default defineAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-6-luna-fast", reasoning: "high", }); ``` For a new scaffold, start the agent again: ```bash npm run dev ``` That's a working agent. Add human-in-the-loop prompts, subagents, and schedules as needed. Follow the [first-agent tutorial](https://eve.dev/docs/tutorial/first-agent) for a complete walkthrough. ### Add Web Chat From your agent's directory, link a Vercel project and add Web Chat: ```bash npx eve link npx eve add channel/web ``` Choose a hosting layout, then **Sign in with Vercel** to provision authentication for members of the project's team. You can also select **Web Chat** from the terminal UI's `/add` channel picker. Run `npx eve deploy` when ready to publish. Local development works without browser sign-in. See the [Web Chat setup guide](https://eve.dev/docs/channels/eve#web-chat-with-sign-in-with-vercel) for permissions and recovery. ## Community The eve community lives on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/eve/discussions), where you can ask questions, share ideas, and show what you've built. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get the repo running locally and land a change, and use [issues](https://github.com/vercel/eve/issues) and [discussions](https://github.com/vercel/eve/discussions) to collaborate. By participating, you agree to our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Security Please do not open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Instead, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and report responsibly to [responsible.disclosure@vercel.com](mailto:responsible.disclosure@vercel.com). ## Beta terms eve is currently in beta and subject to the [Vercel beta terms](https://vercel.com/docs/release-phases/public-beta-agreement); the framework, APIs, documentation, and behavior may change before general availability.
readmeHtml:
eve

eve is a filesystem-first framework for durable AI agents. Core agent capabilities live in conventional locations, so projects are easier to inspect, extend, and operate.

The filesystem is the authoring interface

A typical eve agent has this structure:

my-agent/
└── agent/
    ├── agent.ts            # Optional: model and runtime config
    ├── instructions.md     # Required: the always-on system prompt
    ├── tools/              # Optional: typed functions the model can call
    │   └── get_weather.ts
    ├── skills/             # Optional: procedures loaded on demand
    │   └── plan_a_trip.md
    ├── channels/           # Optional: message channels (HTTP, Slack, Discord)
    │   └── slack.ts
    └── schedules/          # Optional: recurring cron jobs
        └── weekly_recap.ts

Read the documentation for the full project layout and guides.

Quick start

npx eve@latest init my-agent

This creates a new my-agent directory, installs its dependencies, initializes Git, and starts the interactive terminal UI. The generated agent uses openai/gpt-6-luna-fast with high reasoning.

To start with another AI Gateway model, pass its model ID:

npx eve@latest init my-agent --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra

Passing --model without --reasoning uses the provider's default reasoning. Pass --reasoning to set it explicitly.

To add eve to an existing project, pass a path:

cd myapp
npx eve@latest init .

Note

The eve package includes its full documentation, so coding agents can read it locally from node_modules/eve/docs.

A minimal example

The generated project includes an agent directory. Replace agent/instructions.md with:

You are a concise weather demo assistant. Tell users that the weather data is mocked.

Add a mock weather tool at agent/tools/get_weather.ts:

import { defineTool } from "eve/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineTool({
  description: "Return mock weather data for a city.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string().min(1) }),
  async execute({ city }) {
    return { city, condition: "Sunny", temperatureF: 72 };
  },
});

Choose the model in agent/agent.ts:

import { defineAgent } from "eve";

export default defineAgent({
  model: "openai/gpt-6-luna-fast",
  reasoning: "high",
});

For a new scaffold, start the agent again:

npm run dev

That's a working agent. Add human-in-the-loop prompts, subagents, and schedules as needed. Follow the first-agent tutorial for a complete walkthrough.

Add Web Chat

From your agent's directory, link a Vercel project and add Web Chat:

npx eve link
npx eve add channel/web

Choose a hosting layout, then Sign in with Vercel to provision authentication for members of the project's team. You can also select Web Chat from the terminal UI's /add channel picker. Run npx eve deploy when ready to publish. Local development works without browser sign-in. See the Web Chat setup guide for permissions and recovery.

Community

The eve community lives on GitHub Discussions, where you can ask questions, share ideas, and show what you've built.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md to get the repo running locally and land a change, and use issues and discussions to collaborate. By participating, you agree to our Code of Conduct.

Security

Please do not open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Instead, follow SECURITY.md and report responsibly to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com.

Beta terms

eve is currently in beta and subject to the Vercel beta terms; the framework, APIs, documentation, and behavior may change before general availability.

releases.name: eve@0.81.1
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- e4e0cd1: Fix activation trace-content markers to respect the resolved session policy, provider capture settings, and live audience ceiling. Metadata-only sessions now report withheld content accurately without removing content allowed by an explicit trace policy.
- 54d63fd: A session keeps accepting messages during a deployment or compaction handoff, so the first message after a handoff reaches the model sooner and messages sent mid-handoff no longer retry or return `409 session_not_ready`; messages already waiting when a compaction finishes now run before the session moves. Sessions started on an earlier eve release still move to this release: their first move uses the previous handoff, and every move after it uses the new one. On Workflow worlds without hook force-claim support, sessions no longer move between runs, so their run history keeps growing for as long as the session lives.
- fc4dbd0: Cancelling a turn while the model is responding no longer marks its `agent.step` span as an error, so user-initiated stops stop showing up as failures in error tracking.
- 299db19: Connections now accept the documented `auth.displayName` field instead of failing valida

releases.name: eve@0.81.0
releases.body:
### Minor Changes

- e3d1497: Add `github.attribution(ctx)` to `eve/extensions/git` and the deprecated `code({ github })` config. When it returns a `{ name, email }` co-author, the `gh` tool ends every `gh-signed-commit` message and `gh pr create` body with that person's `Co-authored-by` trailer.

### Patch Changes

- 5c53f1f: An approval answer that is neither Approve nor Cancel now gets feedback instead of being dropped, and a repeated answer to an approval that was already decided is discarded before the requester check, so it no longer warns whoever's delivery carried it.
- 4bc7106: Stop reading the parent session's event stream once the remote subagent stream route finds the child's `agent.started` binding. Opening a remote subagent stream no longer replays the rest of a long parent session on every request and retry.
- 932a561: MCP connections close their remote session when the step that opened it ends, instead of leaking one session per step until the process exits. A step that ends while its connection is still connecting, or a sign-in that finishes after its step, can still leave one session open. releases.name: eve@0.80.1
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- a3654ef: Compaction now keeps the start and end of an oversized tool result instead of only its start, so failures, errors, and the `bash` exit code at the end of the output survive.
- 5666d2f: Hosted builds now fail with a clear error when the build output imports a `build.externalDependencies` package, or a subpath of one, that Node's ESM resolver does not resolve to a file inside the output. Previously the build succeeded and the deployed function crashed at boot with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (for example when only a workspace package installed the dependency) or `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` (when the copied version does not export the imported subpath). The error names the import and the app `package.json` to add the package to.
- c1b079c: Publish framework-neutral tracing as `@vercel/agent-runs` with singular `createAgentRun` and `AgentRun` APIs; eve still bundles it without a new runtime dependency. Also fix a development-server build failure in npm-installed apps when generating source maps.

releases.name: eve@0.80.0
releases.body:
### Minor Changes

- 4210766: `git({ github })` accepts an optional `authorize` callback that runs once per `gh` tool invocation with the caller, declared repository, and repository-scoped token; returning `false` blocks the command. It gates caller/repository access, not individual API requests or operations, and allowed commands use the app token's permissions rather than the caller's GitHub permissions.
- 3fea287: Dropped traces and policies excluding either content direction now request Workflow data deletion when the run ends; set `experimental.workflow.retention: "default"` to retain completed transcripts independently of tracing. Expired session-history reads return `410 session_expired` before streaming, including when the World retains purged chunk records.

### Patch Changes

- a5e33ec: Root sessions now accept empty model responses with `finishReason: "stop"` without retrying them or reporting a model-call failure. Recovery for delegated sessions, incomplete streams, and empty non-`stop` responses is unchanged.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open, filesystem-first framework for building and orchestrating AI agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Eve is a robust framework created by Vercel designed to standardize the development and deployment of AI agents. It champions a strict filesystem-first methodology, meaning that agent definitions, capabilities, memory structures, and prompts are managed as standardized files within a repository rather than obscured in database configurations. This approach allows developers to leverage existing version control, CI/CD pipelines, and IDE features seamlessly when building complex, multi-agent systems. The framework provides the underlying infrastructure to connect these file-defined agents with various large language models and external APIs.
keyFeatures: Filesystem-First Design: Mandates that all agent logic, prompts, and configurations are stored as plain text files, enabling robust version control and easy auditing.
Standardized Agent Architecture: Provides a clear, opinionated structure for defining an agent's capabilities, inputs, and expected outputs.
Seamless Vercel Integration: Optimized for deployment on Vercel's infrastructure, allowing developers to spin up agentic workflows with minimal configuration.
Multi-Agent Orchestration: Includes primitives for coordinating complex tasks across multiple specialized agents working in tandem.
Open Framework: Built as an open-source standard to encourage interoperability and community-driven ecosystem growth.

useCases.title: Version-Controlled AI
useCases.description: Engineering teams build AI workflows where every prompt tweak and capability update is reviewed, diffed, and deployed via standard pull requests.

useCases.title: Serverless Agent Deployment
useCases.description: Developers rapidly deploy lightweight, specialized agents to edge functions using Vercel's hosting ecosystem for low-latency responses.

useCases.title: Complex Task Orchestration
useCases.description: Architects design systems where a planner agent delegates sub-tasks to highly specialized researcher and coder agents, all defined within the same repo.

useCases.title: CI/CD AI Testing
useCases.description: QA teams write automated tests against agent definitions stored in the filesystem to ensure behavioral consistency before production deployment.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Eve is for full-stack developers, AI engineers, and DevOps practitioners who want to bring software engineering best practices, such as version control and CI/CD, to the creation of AI agents. Familiarity with agent workflows is highly recommended for optimal usage.
